description: Fragrant, fast-growing herb that loves warmth. A beginner favourite for sunny windowsills and balconies.
care: Pinch the top pair of leaves every 2 weeks to keep it bushy
Let the soil dry slightly between waterings
Remove flower buds to keep leaves tender

problems.name: Yellow lower leaves
problems.solution: Usually overwatering. Let the pot dry out and check drainage.

problems.name: Leggy stems
problems.symptoms: Tall, thin stems with few leaves
problems.solution: Not enough light. Move to the sunniest spot and pinch the tips.

problems.name: Black spots after cold nights
problems.solution: Chill damage below 10 °C. Bring indoors in autumn.

description: Sweet bite-sized tomatoes that crop heavily in containers. Needs warmth, sun, and support.
care: Stake or cage early
Pinch side shoots (suckers) on vining types
Water deeply and evenly to prevent split fruit

problems.name: Aphids on new growth
problems.symptoms: Clusters of small insects, sticky leaves
problems.solution: Spray with mild soapy water every 2–3 days.

problems.name: Blossom end rot
problems.symptoms: Dark sunken patch at the base of fruit
problems.solution: Uneven watering. Keep soil consistently moist and mulch.

problems.name: Split fruit
problems.solution: Pick ripe fruit before storms; water evenly.

description: Quick, cool-season salad leaves. Pick outer leaves and it keeps growing for weeks.
care: Keep soil evenly moist
Thin seedlings to 15–20 cm apart
Harvest outer leaves from 10 cm long

problems.name: Bolting
problems.solution: Heat stress. Grow in spring or fall and give afternoon shade.

problems.name: Slugs
problems.solution: Hand-pick at night; use copper tape on pots.

description: Vigorous perennial herb for teas and drinks. Best kept in its own pot — it spreads!
care: Grow in its own container
Cut back by a third to encourage new growth
Trim to 5 cm before winter

problems.name: Rust spots
problems.solution: Remove affected stems and improve airflow.

description: Cold-hardy leafy green that thrives in cool autumn weather and shrugs off light frost.
care: Sow 1 cm deep, 5 cm apart
Keep evenly moist
Pick outer leaves at 8–10 cm

problems.name: Bolting
problems.solution: Sow in early spring or late summer.

problems.name: Leaf miners
problems.solution: Remove affected leaves; cover with fleece.

description: Bright, citrusy herb that prefers cool weather. Sow little and often.
care: Sow every 3 weeks for a steady supply
Give afternoon shade
Harvest outer stems first

problems.name: Bolting in heat
problems.solution: Grow in spring or fall; it bolts above 27 °C.

description: Tough, nutritious green that gets sweeter after a frost. Harvest leaves all season.
care: Pick lower leaves first
Feed monthly
Net against cabbage worms

problems.name: Cabbage worms
problems.solution: Hand-pick and cover with insect netting.

description: The fastest crop in the garden — crunchy roots in about four weeks.
care: Thin to 5 cm apart
Keep moist for mild flavour
Harvest promptly before they turn woody

problems.name: All leaves, no root
problems.solution: Too crowded or too much nitrogen. Thin early.

description: Peppery salad leaf ready in weeks. Loves cool weather.
care: Cut leaves at 8 cm, it regrows
Sow every 2–3 weeks

problems.name: Flea beetles
problems.solution: Cover with fleece; keep soil moist.

description: Mild onion stalks you can regrow from kitchen scraps on a sunny sill.
care: Snip from the top; leave 3 cm to regrow
Change water every 2 days if regrowing in a jar

problems.name: Thrips
problems.solution: Rinse plants; use sticky traps.

description: Harvest-in-10-days greens grown in a tray indoors any time of year.
care: Sow thickly on moist soil
Mist twice a day
Cut just above the soil when the first true leaves show

problems.name: Mould on the tray
problems.solution: Improve airflow and water from below.

description: Compact, productive beans that need no support. A summer crop.
care: Sow after the last frost
Pick often to keep pods coming

problems.name: Bean beetles
problems.solution: Hand-pick adults and larvae.

description: Compact, colourful plants that thrive in pots. Needs a long warm season.
care: Start indoors 8 weeks before last frost
Let soil dry slightly between waterings

problems.name: Flower drop
problems.solution: Temperatures too high or low; shake to pollinate indoors.

description: Perennial berries for hanging baskets and pots. Plant in spring for summer fruit.
care: Plant crowns level with the soil
Remove runners for bigger fruit
Mulch with straw

problems.name: Grey mould
problems.solution: Remove affected fruit; keep berries off the soil.

description: Sweet, crunchy pods on climbing vines. One of the first crops of spring.
care: Give a trellis to climb
Pick pods daily once they start

problems.name: Powdery mildew
problems.solution: Improve airflow; water at the base.

description: Sweet roots for deep containers. Short varieties suit balconies.
care: Use a pot at least 30 cm deep
Keep the surface moist until seedlings appear
Thin to 5 cm apart

problems.name: Forked roots
problems.solution: Stony or compacted soil; use loose potting mix.

description: Fresh, mild herb that keeps producing from spring to the first hard frost.
care: Soak seeds overnight; they are slow to sprout
Cut outer stems at the base so the centre keeps growing

problems.name: Green and black caterpillars
problems.solution: Swallowtail larvae. Hand-pick them or move them to a spare plant.

description: Hardy onion-flavoured herb that comes back every spring.
care: Snip leaves 2 cm above the soil
Divide crowded clumps every 3 years

problems.name: Thrips
problems.solution: Rinse the plant and use blue or yellow sticky traps.

description: Feathery herb for pickles and fish; its flowers attract helpful insects.
care: Sow where it will grow; it dislikes transplanting
Sow again every 3 weeks for a steady supply

problems.name: Bolting
problems.symptoms: Flower heads form quickly in heat
problems.solution: Harvest leaves young and keep sowing small batches.

description: Low, woody perennial herb that loves sun and dry soil.
care: Let the soil dry out between waterings
Trim lightly after flowering to keep it compact

problems.name: Root rot
problems.symptoms: Stems turn brown and soft at the base
problems.solution: Too wet. Use gritty, well-drained soil and water less.

description: Easy perennial herb for pizza and pasta; tastes strongest in full sun.
care: Pinch off flower buds for the best flavour
Cut back by a third in midsummer

problems.name: Root rot
problems.solution: Let the soil dry between waterings and check drainage.

description: Fragrant woody herb. Not winter-hardy in zone 5b, so grow it in a pot and bring it in.
care: Start from a young plant; seeds are slow
Bring the pot indoors before nights drop below -5 °C

problems.name: Powdery mildew indoors
problems.symptoms: White powder on leaves in winter
problems.solution: Give it a sunny window, airflow and drier soil.

description: Silvery perennial herb that is very drought-tolerant once established.
care: Harvest lightly in the first year
Prune woody stems back in spring

problems.name: Powdery mildew
problems.solution: Space plants for airflow and water at the base.

description: Lemon-scented perennial for tea. Spreads like mint, so keep it in a pot.
care: Cut stems back by half when it gets leggy
Remove flowers to stop it self-seeding

problems.name: Powdery mildew
problems.symptoms: White powder on leaves late in summer
problems.solution: Cut it back hard; fresh growth comes back clean.

description: Colourful stems and big leaves; one sowing crops from summer into autumn.
care: Pick outer leaves and leave the centre
Each seed is a cluster, so thin to one seedling

problems.name: Leaf miners
problems.symptoms: Pale tunnels or blotches inside the leaves
problems.solution: Remove affected leaves and cover the crop with fleece.

description: Fast cool-season green for stir-fries; harvest as baby leaves or whole heads.
care: Grow in spring or late summer, not midsummer
Keep the soil evenly moist

problems.name: Bolting
problems.symptoms: Flower stalk appears in hot weather
problems.solution: Sow in cool months and harvest promptly.

problems.name: Flea beetles
problems.symptoms: Tiny shot holes in the leaves
problems.solution: Cover with fleece right after sowing.

description: Peppery greens that grow fast and handle cold well.
care: Pick leaves young for a milder taste
Sow every 3 weeks in cool weather

problems.name: Aphids
problems.symptoms: Clusters of small insects under leaves
problems.solution: Spray with water or mild soapy water.

description: Large, sturdy leaves that taste sweeter after frost.
care: Harvest the lowest leaves first
Grow in a large pot or bed; plants get big

problems.name: Cabbage worms
problems.solution: Hand-pick and cover with fine netting.

description: Fast summer crop. Bush or trellised types suit balconies.
care: Grow up a trellis to save space
Pick every 2 days so the plant keeps fruiting

problems.name: Powdery mildew
problems.solution: Water at the base and remove the worst leaves.

problems.name: Bitter fruit
problems.solution: Heat or dry soil stress. Water deeply and evenly.

description: One plant feeds a family all summer. Needs space and a big container.
care: Pick fruit at 15–20 cm, before it gets huge
Use a container of at least 40 litres

problems.name: Powdery mildew
problems.solution: Normal late in summer. Remove bad leaves and improve airflow.

problems.name: Sudden wilting
problems.symptoms: Whole plant collapses, sawdust at the stem base
problems.solution: Squash vine borer. Cover young plants and check stems in June.

description: Sweet peppers for warm, sunny spots. Start indoors early.
care: Start seeds indoors 8 weeks before the last frost
Stake plants once fruit sets

problems.name: Blossom end rot
problems.symptoms: Dark sunken patch at the bottom of fruit
problems.solution: Uneven watering. Keep soil evenly moist and mulch.

description: Heat-loving fruiting crop; compact varieties suit pots.
care: Plant out only when nights stay above 15 °C
Harvest while the skin is still glossy

problems.name: Flea beetles
problems.solution: Cover young plants with fleece until they flower.

description: Cool-season crop; after the main head, side shoots keep coming.
care: Cut the main head while the buds are tight
Leave the plant to grow side shoots

problems.name: Cabbage worms
problems.solution: Cover with fine netting and soak heads in salt water before cooking.

description: Dense heads for slaw and soups; grows best in spring or autumn.
care: Keep soil evenly moist so heads do not split
Harvest when the head feels firm

problems.name: Split heads
problems.solution: Harvest firm heads promptly and water evenly.

description: Rewarding but fussy: needs steady moisture and cool weather.
care: Tie leaves over the head to keep it white
Never let the plant dry out

problems.name: Tiny heads (buttoning)
problems.solution: Stress from heat, drought or root damage. Transplant young and water steadily.

description: Grow from sets for an easy start; long-day types suit northern gardens.
care: Plant sets with the tips just showing
Stop watering when the tops fall over

problems.name: Onion thrips
problems.solution: Rinse plants and avoid crowding.

description: Plant cloves in autumn and harvest the next summer. Almost no care.
care: Plant cloves 5 cm deep, pointed end up, in October
Cut off the curly flower stalks (scapes) in June

problems.name: Rotting cloves
problems.symptoms: Soft bulbs, yellow leaves in spring
problems.solution: Soil too wet. Plant in raised, well-drained beds.

description: Thirsty, slow crop that rewards steady care with crisp stalks.
care: Never let the soil dry out
Pick outer stalks as needed

problems.name: Stringy, hollow stalks
problems.solution: Dry soil. Water daily in warm weather and mulch.

description: Mild onion relative that stands in the garden well into winter.
care: Plant seedlings in deep holes
Pile soil around the stems for long white shanks

problems.name: Leek rust
problems.solution: Remove affected leaves and give plants more airflow.

description: Sweet roots and edible leaves; fine in a deep pot.
care: Each seed is a cluster, so thin to one seedling
Harvest when roots are golf-ball to tennis-ball size

problems.name: Woody roots
problems.solution: Left too long or dry soil. Harvest young and water evenly.

description: Quick cool-season roots; the greens are edible too.
care: Harvest roots at 5–8 cm across
Sow in late summer for a sweet autumn crop

problems.name: Flea beetles
problems.solution: Cover with fleece after sowing.

description: Fun in grow bags: keep adding soil and dig up a surprise harvest.
care: Plant seed potatoes, not supermarket ones
Pile soil over the stems as they grow

problems.name: Green potatoes
problems.solution: Light exposure makes them toxic. Keep tubers covered and do not eat green parts.

problems.name: Colorado potato beetle
problems.symptoms: Striped beetles and red larvae eating leaves
problems.solution: Hand-pick daily and check under leaves for eggs.

description: Slow, sweet roots that taste best after the first frosts.
care: Use fresh seed every year
Wear gloves when handling the leaves; the sap can irritate skin in sun

problems.name: Forked roots
problems.solution: Stony or compacted soil. Use deep, loose soil.

description: Grown from rooted slips; loves heat and makes pretty vines.
care: Plant slips two weeks after the last frost
Dig before the first frost and cure them warm for 10 days

problems.name: Cracked roots
problems.solution: Uneven watering. Water deeply once a week.

description: Climbing beans that crop for weeks on a small footprint.
care: Put the trellis up before sowing
Pick every 2–3 days while pods are slim

problems.name: Mexican bean beetle
problems.solution: Hand-pick beetles and yellow larvae under the leaves.

description: Cold-hardy beans to sow in early spring.
care: Sow as soon as the soil can be worked
Pinch out the tips once the first pods form

problems.name: Black aphids
problems.symptoms: Black insects on the growing tips
problems.solution: Pinch out the infested tips.

description: Green soybeans picked young; a fun, protein-rich crop.
care: Sow after the soil warms up
Harvest when pods are plump and still bright green

problems.name: Japanese beetles
problems.solution: Knock them into soapy water in the early morning.

description: Perennial canes; autumn-fruiting types crop in the first year.
care: Plant bare-root canes in early spring
Cut autumn-fruiting canes to the ground in late winter

problems.name: Japanese beetles
problems.solution: Hand-pick in the early morning.

description: Long-lived bushes that need acidic soil; great in containers.
care: Use acidic potting mix (pH 4.5–5.5)
Grow two varieties for better fruit set

problems.name: Yellow leaves with green veins
problems.solution: Soil not acidic enough. Use an acidifying feed or sulfur.

description: Sweet melons for hot summers; small varieties grow on a sturdy trellis.
care: Support fruit on a trellis with slings
Ripe melons slip off the vine with a gentle push

problems.name: Powdery mildew
problems.solution: Water at the base and give the vines airflow.
